title: Mitigate SLO pager storms via transient spike attenuation and priority bucketing
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: During a capacity regression on 2025-02-12 we experienced a cascade of burn-rate pagers that overwhelmed the on-call rotation and obscured high-impact incidents. Root causes identified in the postmortem: (1) autoscaler oscillation caused transient traffic spikes; (2) a recent KV-cache invalidation regression increased 95th/99th latency for short-lived chat requests, amplifying burn rates; (3) current pagering policies aggressively escalate short-duration burn spikes without a transient-smoothing layer.

Goals: introduce safeguards so short transient spikes (sub-10m) do not trigger full-page storms while preserving fast escalation for genuine sustained SLO breaches. Reduce noisy pages by >70% for transient events in the next quarter while keeping mean time to detect high-severity regressions within current SLOs.

Artifacts: postmortem doc: https://confluence.internal.redwood/slo-postmortem-2025-02-12, KV-cache regression PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7853, initial alert-policy RFC: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1XgSLO-attenuate-rfc
actions: Action 1: Implement a transient-windowed burn smoothing algorithm in alert pipeline (10m decay + max-peak hold). Owner: Liam O'Connor. Due: 2025-03-08. Deliverable: config flag + unit tests + rollout plan.

Action 2: Add priority bucketing to burn-rate alerts so low-priority customers/route-level synthetic traffic are de-emphasized during short spikes. Owner: Priya Nair. Due: 2025-03-12. Deliverable: mapping table + console UI for bucket edits.

Action 3: Tweak pagering thresholds to require sustained burn above threshold for 5m before full paging, with staged notify (Slack -> Email -> Pager). Owner: Oncall Platform. Due: 2025-03-05. Deliverable: new escalation policy and playbook updates.

Action 4: Fix KV-cache invalidation regression and add regression test covering cold-KV invalidation tail latency. Owner: Ricardo Alvarez (runtime). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7898. Due: 2025-02-28.

Action 5: Add a lightweight classifier to suppress pages for autocorrelated spikes caused by autoscaler churn (heuristic-based initial version). Owner: SRE Machine Learning. Due: 2025-03-20. Deliverable: experimental service + A/B evaluation metrics.
Action 6: Update runbook/playbook with steps to identify genuine vs noisy burn events and provide a 'mute for 15m' operator button in Console. Owner: Developer Experience. Due: 2025-03-15.
Action 7: Run a 2-week canary of new alert pipeline with staged rollout to reduce blast radius. Owner: Reliability Eng. Due: 2025-03-22. Deliverable: canary dashboard and rollback plan.
acceptance_criteria: Pager volume for transient capacity spikes reduced by >= 70% in canary region compared to baseline (30d pre-change).
No increase in time-to-detect for sustained SLO breaches (<= 10% regression vs baseline).
Clear playbook and operator controls published in Console and Confluence.
All new configs are feature-flagged and have rollback paths; e2e tests and unit tests added to CI.
